claude.rationale: This is a whole-company, all-cash going-private reverse triangular merger: Merger Sub merged into Envision with the entire corporate entity and its subsidiaries surviving intact as an indirect subsidiary of a KKR-affiliated Parent, so the legal vehicle, business model, product, processes, and people all crossed the boundary together as one going concern (gap_45=0). The customer-facing physician-services product and its operational "Affiliated Medical Group" management-services structure were expressly preserved "as an ongoing feature of the surviving company rather than something altered by the merger," so product and its producing processes moved together (gap_45=0). Section 5.6 built in contractual one-year workforce and compensation continuity ("no less favorable," "substantially comparable"), so the processes and the organization/people that run them transferred together (gap_56=0). T1 coded replace because a financial sponsor (KKR, via newly formed shell entities) installed new controlling ownership over the going-private company, replacing the prior public-shareholder controlling intent.

gemini.rationale: The transaction was a whole-company going-private acquisition by KKR. The entire corporate entity, its physician-services operating model (T4/T5), and its workforce (T6) were transferred intact, with contractual continuity for employees and preservation of the 'Affiliated Medical Group' structure, resulting in no structural gaps at closing.

grok.rationale: The slice documents a whole-company reverse triangular merger in which Merger Sub merged into Envision and Envision survived as an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of KKR-controlled Parent, with the entire corporate entity and subsidiaries as the transaction subject rather than a carved-out unit. Customer-facing physician-services product and the Affiliated Medical Group management-services operating structure were expressly preserved intact in the surviving company, so T4 and T5 crossed together with no product-vs-process mismatch at closing. Contractual one-year continuing-employee compensation and benefits continuity was built into the merger agreement (Section 5.6), so T5 and T6 likewise transferred/aligned together with no process-vs-organization structural gap at closing.
